answer: Picture a shared reward pot split by similarity. Every epoch peers pose the same fable to a random sample of agents, ask each to retell it, and cluster the replies by reasoning and style. Agents whose retellings land in one cluster split a single share, like facets cut from one onyx stone. To earn twice, a second identity must truly wander off in thought, which means a different model, prompt and memory to run and maintain, so each extra head adds a full new cost.
